<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **182** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 815e882be935fadd2d6edd77216fb9d437d58ce8` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b7df48177cd80eb2b202c79cdb6544880e55ddaa` — the merge of head `b1d5a7f45975f1f731ce52a42495fabbccf78c26` into base `815e882be935fadd2d6edd77216fb9d437d58ce8`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b7df48177cd80eb2b202c79cdb6544880e55ddaa && git checkout b7df48177cd80eb2b202c79cdb6544880e55ddaa
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 815e882be935fadd2d6edd77216fb9d437d58ce8 b1d5a7f45975f1f731ce52a42495fabbccf78c26 && git checkout -B drift-repro 815e882be935fadd2d6edd77216fb9d437d58ce8 && git merge --no-ff b1d5a7f45975f1f731ce52a42495fabbccf78c26

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 815e882be935fadd2d6edd77216fb9d437d58ce8
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 815e882be935fadd2d6edd77216fb9d437d58ce8` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c213f8fb80de083b3dfde0d7dcb3b63af1439c31`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/automation/builtin-node-config.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/19.flow-variable-key-reserved-segment-refused.ts + packages/services/service-automation/src/scope-key-segments.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-registration-checks.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/run-resume.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/dag-traversal.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/variable-key-reserved-segments.test.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/run-values-isolation.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/flow-condition-scope-keys.dogfood.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts
Security-touching: yes
Rule-change-verified: none

Inputs: the governing ruling (two halves: the door, and P2), the PR body, its 14-file list, the net diff `02ed8408450..c213f8fb80d`, and the head's check-runs. Read-only: every statement below is read from the tree at the head; nothing was built or run. Prose faces (`.changeset/automation-variable-keys-reserved-segments.md`, `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`) read for ② and accuracy only. Mechanism-level detail is held privately with the security seat; this record stays at the rule.

Gate verdicts: every completed check-run on this head is `success` or `skipped`, except the first `Check Changeset` run (`failure`, 15:04Z), superseded by the later one (`success`, 16:34Z), which governs.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Authored flows that change answer.** One check, `validateVariableKeySegments`, sits in the shared `registrationChecks` list, so `registerFlow` and the stored pass judge one set by construction. It judges, in every graph `collectFlowGraphs` returns: each declared variable's `name`; an `assignment` node's targets in the three shapes its executor reads; `outputVariable` / `iteratorVariable` / `indexVariable` / `errorVariable` on a node of any type; each `screen` `fields[].name`. A flow naming a key with one of the three words as its name or as a dot-separated part moves from registered to refused, every site named.
- **Nothing refused beyond the three words.** The match is exact per part after a split on `.`: `constructor_name`, `prototype_count` and a differently-cased spelling are untouched (the control cases pin the first two, at registration, on a run and on a resume). Two small supersets, both inside "a key the flow names": the four `…Variable` keys are judged on every node type whether or not that type binds them, and a degenerate legacy-array entry is judged by a slightly wider name pick than the executor's (N3).
- **The judged set is not every key a flow names** — see M1.
- **Resume calls that change answer.** Every key of `output` and of `variables` (the REST body's `inputs` and its alias, the MCP resume's values) with such a part now answers `INVALID_SIGNAL` (400). For `output` that is accepted → refused. For `inputs` on a screen with declared fields it is a change of code inside the same 400 (`INVALID_SCREEN_INPUT` → `INVALID_SIGNAL`), as the updated dogfood pin states. Engine-built continuation signals are judged too (S1).
- **P2 is a behaviour change, not an accept-set change**: a declared object or list default is copied per run; a dotted write under a held value lands in a copy the expression scope owns; an in-memory suspension is handed out with its own `variables`.
- **Spec prose edits change no shape and no generated artifact.** The two hunks in `builtin-node-config.zod.ts` are `//` comments (no `.describe()` text); the hunk in `automation-service.ts` is one JSDoc paragraph on `AutomationResult.code`. `INVALID_SIGNAL` is an existing code that gains a documented cause; it is already in the retryable-refusal set, so a delegating parent stays parked on it.
- **The ledger entry is reachable as the gate expects.** Semantic entries are discovered by directory (the registry is generated); the file sits beside its `19.*` siblings, matches the spec's `19.0.0-next.0` step, and carries no `relevantWhen`, which is right for a surface that includes a runtime request body. The changeset marker names its id; the ledger-synchrony gates and the latest `Check Changeset` run are green on this head.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/service-automation: minor` with a `!` title and two `BREAKING` bullets: the level this repo's sibling narrowings carry on the 19 line (`35143-data-model-publish-checks.md`, `36595-related-list-key-under-arrangement.md`). Holds.
- `@objectstack/spec: patch` for prose plus one registered ledger entry: the same pairing those siblings use. Holds. `@objectstack/runtime: patch` covers a comment-only hunk; harmless.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` holds: no hunk widens an accept set or adds a capability. `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` holds: authorable flow metadata that registered is now refused, with no schema shape change.
- ADR-0087 `registered flow-variable-key-reserved-segment-refused`: marker, entry id and file agree. The entry's `surface`, `replacement` and `reason` state the rule only. Its `acceptanceCriteria` ("`os migrate meta --stored` lists no flow with such a key") can be met while a flow M1 covers is still affected; it becomes exact when M1 is fixed.
- FROM → TO: the first two bullets carry FROM, TO and the fix. Two accuracy points: N2 (the resume bullet's FROM) and S4 (the third bullet's "Nothing to change").

### ③ Boundary flags

- **(a) Registration sites.** Declared names, assignment targets in all three shapes, the four `…Variable` keys and screen field names are judged, and the stored pass reads the same check. **Not every site is**: M1.
- **(b) Resume.** The refusal is the first statement after the suspension is loaded and any delegation is resolved, ahead of `refuseInvalidScreenInput` (the screen contract and its `visibleWhen`) and ahead of `applyResumeSignal`. Nothing earlier reads a caller's `output` or `variables` (the one earlier reader answers on the engine's own marker first). It returns before the suspension is consumed, so the run stays paused. `applyResumeSignal` refuses the same keys as a whole, and both of its callers are covered. Every door found reaching it (the REST resume route, the MCP resume, the wait-node timers, a caller's signal delegated down to a subflow child) goes through `resume` → `resumeInternal`. Holds for caller signals; for the engine's own signals see S1.
- **(c) P2 copies.** Defaults: deep-copied at seeding, arrays and plain objects at every depth. Dotted writes: the scope tracks the containers it made per build and descends into a one-level copy of anything else, so every write lands in an object the scope owns; a list stays a list, any other object becomes a prototype-free copy. Held runs: the only two direct reads of the in-memory cache both go through the copy. **One path still shares a held object**: S2. Cost: one shallow copy per held object per scope build, and only when a dotted key descends into it; one deep copy per object/list default per run; one deep copy of all variables per in-memory load, on engines with no store or a run the store never took. Linear and acceptable; N1 for one edge.
- **(d) Authoring lint door.** `os validate` and `FlowSchema.parse` do not apply the rule: the spec comments in this diff say so in words ("this schema accepts"). The ruling names registration, the stored pass and resume, so it is not owed here. **Residual R1**: an author meets the rule at registration, not at validate; a lint rule is a follow-up for the security seat to file.
- **Dev flag — "node ids are not judged by the authoring door".** Answered in part, escalated in part. A node id heads every key a node's output is stored under, and this same file's existing enumeration of names a node binds (`flowNodeBoundNames`) counts it. Whether the ruling's "variable keys" takes node ids in is a contract call: **escalated to the security seat**, not decided here. Whichever way it goes, the two doors must give one answer for one key (S1).
- **Dev flag — "a security item is with the owner seat".** Noted; nothing to answer on the public face.
- **Author.** `objectstack-fleet[bot]`. No auto-merge is armed on this head (the PR is a draft), so no disarm is owed.
- **SQL push-down (AGENTS.md).** n/a: the diff adds no data access, no id materialisation and no in-app join.

### ④ Design judgment

The ruling, sentence by sentence.

- **"Variable keys cannot use a reserved segment as the whole name or any dot-separated part."** The predicate is right: exact match per part, empty parts included. Bracketed and indexed spellings are either refused by a dotted part or are one literal segment that no scope walk reads as a path (both walks split on `.` only). Case variants and look-alike code points are different property names and are correctly left alone.
- **"Refused at flow registration and in the stored pass."** One check, two readers: the same set by construction. The set itself falls short.
  - M1 (must-fix) — on two authoring shapes a flow that names a key with a reserved segment still registers and is not listed by the stored pass. On one of them the flow then binds such a key at run time; on the other it registers and pauses, and no submission can complete it. Held privately with the security seat. The changeset, the docs page and the ledger entry say registration judges every key a flow names; that sentence is not true at this head.
- **"Refused in a resume signal before anything reads the submitted values, the run staying paused."** Holds for every caller signal, at the first check and again at the chokepoint.
  - S1 (should-fix) — the chokepoint judges the engine's own continuation signals on the stated ground that their keys are names the authoring door already holds (`reservedResumeSignalKeys` docblock). That ground does not hold for every key the engine builds: on one flow shape the door registers, the engine's own continuation is refused and the run parks with no valid submission able to move it. Held privately with the security seat. Tied to the node-id escalation in ③.
- **"One run's writes never change a flow's declared defaults, the trigger's record or another run's values."** Defaults: held on every path read (seeding copy, dotted writes, a node that changes the value in place, the next run). Another run's values through a pause: held with and without a store.
  - S2 (should-fix) — for the trigger's record the rule is held for a dotted write and for a run resumed from a pause, and not on one further path. Held privately with the security seat. The docs page and the changeset state the wider rule without that limit; either the tree or the prose moves, and which is the ruling's to say.
- **Keys produced at run time rather than authored** (a trigger record's own field names, a node's output keys): no door judges them, by design; what holds for them is the scope rule (prototype-free containers, the skipped segment) plus this diff's copy on descent. Named as **residual R2**, not a finding.
- **Would the pins catch a regression?** Resume: yes for caller signals — six samples on a screen (the conditions never evaluated, the paused variables byte-identical, the valid submission landing), on a pause with no input contract, at the chokepoint, and through the HTTP route in the dogfood pin. P2: defaults, the record's dotted write, and a pause with and without a store.
  - S3 (should-fix) — the authoring pin does not hold the door's site list. Its nine cases cover declared names, the assignment map and bare shapes, one `outputVariable` and one screen field. There is no case for the legacy-array assignment shape, `iteratorVariable`, `indexVariable`, `errorVariable` or a key inside a nested graph, and no enumeration pin against the spec's own list of binding positions; removing any of those branches leaves both new files green. The resume side has no case for a signal delegated to a subflow child or for an engine-built signal.
  - S4 (should-fix, prose) — the changeset's third bullet ends "Nothing to change" and the docs say a dotted write "is read back by that run". The two scope builders differ: an expression reads the write back from the scope's copy; a text hole over the same path reads the held value, because the text scope never merges a flat key into a variable. A flow that read a dotted write through a text hole or through `$record` changes on upgrade; the bullet should say which reader reads it back and carry a FROM → TO.
  - N1 (nit) — `copyHeldValue` has no guard for a value that refers to itself; a suspension holding one fails its in-memory load, reported under a store-unavailable code on an engine with no store. `SuspendedRun` documents its fields as JSON-serialisable, so this is outside the stated contract.
  - N2 (nit) — the resume bullet's "FROM: such a key was accepted" is exact for `output`; for `inputs` on a screen with declared fields the call was already a 400 under another code.
  - N3 (nit) — the door picks a legacy-array entry's name as "the first of `variable` / `name` / `key` that is a non-empty string"; the executor and the spec's `flowAssignmentTargets` pick "the first that is not null". The door is the superset, so nothing slips; it can refuse an entry the executor binds nothing for.

One must-fix (M1), four should-fix (S1–S4), three nits. The resume door and the default-isolation half hold as ruled; the authoring door does not yet refuse every key a flow names, so the narrowing is not delivered whole at this head.
